svg.title: Two forms of intelligence
svg.desc: Schematic comparison of two approaches. A five-axis radar shows the rebuild drawn larger than a model on every task on energy per correct result, determinism, verification strength, reuse and compounding, and independence from models; no values are plotted. A line chart shows bolt-on cost per task flat each round while rebuild cost falls to a handler floor. A second chart shows model weights as a sawtooth that resets each release while a library of promoted solutions climbs in steps. A table contrasts where intelligence lives, how it grows, what a task costs, what trust rests on, and what intelligence is. A references block at the bottom gives sources; unreferenced wording is labelled informed opinion.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, DejaVu Sans, sans-serif
IBM Plex Sans, DejaVu Sans, sans-serif
text.tspan: The bolt-on keeps intelligence in weights that must be re-run every time. The rebuild keeps it in a verified library that is paid for once. Both
diagrams are qualitative: shapes of the argument, not measurements.
